title: The lib owns the record-domain laws; commands render
rationale: The lib is fabro natively embedded (README product posture): an embedder must validate records and classify staleness without shelling out. Pre-C1 both laws lived as pub(crate) CLI modules with an inverted dependency (full_verdict called up into commands::hint_fields) - five CLI consumers, zero embedder reach. Byte-neutral move, proven by the differential battery.

description: jiff Span constructors PANIC on out-of-range fields: Span::new().hours(n) panics for |n| > 175,307,616 (jiff-0.2 span.rs range check) — so saturating an i64 day count into Span::hours() trades an overflow panic for a RANGE panic, and Timestamp + Span panics on out-of-range results (the checked_add variant returns Result). Sprint-21 standards-review blocker: StaleRule::verdict computed (days + 1) * 24 as Span::hours for a shelf that could saturate at i64::MAX (absurd config) — debug panic, release wrap to 0 hours → EVERY record Stale (verdict inversion). RULE: timestamp math over possibly-huge values belongs in plain i64 seconds/milliseconds (now.as_millisecond() - recorded.as_millisecond(), saturating the boundary) — exact, overflow-proof, and byte-identical to the reference's Math.floor millisecond semantics. Reserve jiff Span arithmetic for values known to be small.
resolution: Compare timestamps in plain i64 milliseconds (now.as_millisecond() - recorded.as_millisecond() >= (days+1).saturating_mul(86_400_000)) — exact and overflow-proof; Timestamp::checked_add returns Result for the Span path, but avoid the Span construction entirely for possibly-huge values. Pinned by a saturation unit test (i64::MAX days -> Fresh).
